context: Request: across the M&A practice (including deals in negotiation, JV formations, minority investments), how often signed deals carry a fraud carve-out from indemnification caps and baskets, and which deals. Rubric: 27 qualifying matters (1001-00003 … 1046-00001), a rate criterion (27 of 35 M&A matters, about 77%), and a precision criterion.

stages.stage: List files in the document store
stages.note: Whole-store glob plus a shallow find that prints nothing.

stages.stage: Search file names for request keywords
stages.note: find | grep over file paths for deal-document words, first 300 hits only.

stages.stage: Screen candidate matters by reading documents
stages.note: Reads the first 400 lines of six executed agreements from six matters on that list.

stages.stage: Read a chosen matter's documents in depth
stages.note: Reads the next 500 lines of the same six agreements.

stages.stage: Screen candidate matters by reading documents
stages.note: Reads agreements, memos and an issues list from five further matters on the list.

stages.stage: Read a chosen matter's documents in depth
stages.note: Reads later sections of four agreements, plus a memo and draft of one new candidate (labelled by the dominant intent).

stages.stage: Write the response
stages.note: Writes a five-of-five rate over the signed agreements it read.

stages.stage: Finish the run
stages.note: Calls finish.

runs.sequence: List files in the document store → Search file names for request keywords → Screen candidate matters by reading documents → Read a chosen matter's documents in depth → Screen candidate matters by reading documents → Read a chosen matter's documents in depth → Write the response → Finish the run
runs.failure_point: Its only search was a capped file-name list; it read about ten matters from it and reported a rate over five agreements.

first_error.stage: Search file names for request keywords
first_error.why: Its one search was a file-name list cut at 300 lines that reached five of the 27 qualifying matters, and it never ran a store-wide content search or widened the list.

stages.stage: List files in the document store
stages.note: Whole-store glob.

stages.stage: Read documents picked from the file listing
stages.note: Reads agreements, a redline and an issues list of the two matters at the top of the listing.

stages.stage: Search within a candidate matter's files
stages.note: Two greps inside those matters with a non-recursive glob (both empty), plus two reads, one at a guessed path.

stages.stage: Read a chosen matter's documents in depth
tags: run ended: text reply without finish
stages.note: Reads later sections of the two agreements; the run then ends with the answer as a chat message and no file written.

runs.sequence: List files in the document store → Read documents picked from the file listing → Search within a candidate matter's files → Read a chosen matter's documents in depth
runs.failure_point: It read only the two matters at the top of the listing, and ended the run with the answer as chat text and no response file.

first_error.stage: Read documents picked from the file listing
first_error.why: It chose what to read from the two matters at the top of a capped listing and never searched the store, so it counted one signed deal.

other_errors.stage: Read a chosen matter's documents in depth
other_errors.why: It ended the turn with the answer as a chat message instead of writing the response file and calling finish, so the judge saw no output.

stages.stage: List files in the document store
stages.note: Four whole-store globs by file type (one type has no files).

stages.stage: Read documents picked from the file listing
stages.note: Reads agreements, memos and an issues list of the two matters at the top of the listing.

stages.stage: Scan document text with an extraction script
stages.note: Extraction script over agreements with two specific file-name patterns across the store, printing matching clauses.

stages.stage: Search file names for request keywords
stages.note: Six file-name globs for deal-structure words; two return nothing.

stages.stage: Screen candidate matters by reading documents
stages.note: Reads the openings of five agreements from four matters on those lists.

stages.stage: Scan document text with an extraction script
stages.note: Two store-wide extraction scripts for deal-structure and clause terms; both time out, the second after about 196K chars.

stages.stage: Write the response
stages.note: Writes a twelve-of-twelve rate and also lists negotiation and other matters outside the signed set.

stages.stage: Finish the run
stages.note: Calls finish.

runs.sequence: List files in the document store → Read documents picked from the file listing → Scan document text with an extraction script → Search file names for request keywords → Screen candidate matters by reading documents → Scan document text with an extraction script → Write the response → Finish the run
runs.failure_point: Both store-wide scans timed out part-way; it wrote a rate over the twelve agreements in the partial output and also asserted extra matters.

first_error.stage: Scan document text with an extraction script
first_error.why: Both store-wide scans timed out before covering the store and it wrote the answer from the partial output without narrowing or rerunning them.

other_errors.why: The answer presents negotiation, JV and other matters outside the qualifying set as qualifying examples.

divergence: All three runs reached only a fraction of the 27 qualifying matters, by different routes. T0 relied on one capped file-name list (search miss); T1 read only the two matters at the top of the listing and then ended without writing a file (partial listing as corpus, no deliverable); T2's store-wide scans timed out and it wrote from the partial output (search miss), also asserting extra matters. All three reported a near-100% rate over a small set.
